cycleBound.rule: One review and at most one narrow re-check per judge, the re-check only for blockers that are new, narrow and runtime-only

blockers.what: An EQUIPMENT_CHANGE of the same week still erases a return that starts next week (the handler re-projects from the pre-break state and never reads the stored return); the opposite order keeps it. SSCTR O-1/R28 is the same handler after a weekly review
blockers.status: PARTIAL (weekly review, schedule change, goal change fixed)

blockers.what: SHORT-class return: reported on the morning of a quality day, the first run back stays the quality run (the SHORT rule still compares dates only); the SSCTR's R27 (non-blocking for the science) is the same case
After a return in race week that re-plans from next week, postponing the race leaves the old race in place: two races; the opposite order gives one
blockers.status: PARTIAL (race moved earlier and race postponed in race week fixed)

blockers.what: The per-exercise merge keeps one whole entry, so a known load is replaced by an unknown one when the other entry has as many known values; over ten weeks four exercises are never established (field-by-field merge needed)
blockers.status: PARTIAL (subset report, no-load report, label prefix, drift fixed)

blockers.what: A shortfall logged one or two increments lighter than the plan still becomes the repetition target (3x3 at 77.5 kg, 3x2 at 75 kg, below the goal range [4, 6])
blockers.status: PARTIAL (shortfall at the planned load fixed)

blockers.what: An event change that reaches this week discards that week's earlier same-week adaptations (systemic-fatigue reduction, unavailable-day reschedule): the rebuild from the current week re-projects from the week-start state
blockers.status: NEW, introduced by the second cycle (QE-R7A-03 fix)

blockers.what: A week whose executed exposures were all fitted to the time budget below their count counts as a whole executed week, so it raises or ends the regain cap; with a later budget increase the count rises more than one set above the largest executed count (2, 2, then 4 sets). Required: the caps rise or end only after a week in which an executed exposure did its whole count after its time fit
blockers.status: NEW, introduced by the second cycle (QE-R7A-14 reading for the caps); under Founder §16 it also keeps D53 from closing

regression.classification: REGRESSION / CHALLENGE REUSE; not generalization evidence

nextEngineeringStep.recommended: A bounded, Founder-authorized follow-up for the seven named blockers before R7-B: one same-week composition model (every same-week handler starts from the week as currently prescribed and from the stored return state), a field-by-field merge of agreeing reports, a fit-aware whole-count test for the caps, and the lighter-load shortfall and SHORT-return cases; then a new freeze with a narrow re-check by both judges
